anchors.cell_block_centre: origin on the centre of a cell block at floor level (ground tiles, floors, courts, pyramids)
anchors.cell_centre: origin on one cell's centre at floor level (stairs, slopes, causeways)
anchors.cell_edge: origin on a cell boundary line at floor level (walls straddle it; cliffs stand on it facing south)
anchors.corner: origin on a cell corner at floor level (piers)
anchors.door_anchor: origin on the room.gd door anchor: 0.4 m in from the room edge = 0.1 m inside the wall centre line
anchors.free: footprint-centred free prop (statues, columns, obelisks, altars, nature)
anchors.wall_face: origin on a wall's face at floor level (banners, vines)

connectors.rule: walls, ramparts and cliffs meet end to end on cell boundaries
ground tiles meet edge to edge on the datum (edges stay at y = 0)
a pier covers the joint where two walls meet on a cell corner
a door socket takes exactly one ruin.gate frame (room.gd places it from the room's door data via the arch.door binding); ruin.gate__sealed is the closed state
a stair flight's foot on a cell edge at the lower level, its top on the far edge
a pyramid's stair foot meets the approach paving
slopes chain terrace levels cell by cell
wall-face props hang on wall sockets
the oasis bank rim lies on the ground datum (water at -0.25 m)
a terrace top edge takes a land.slope crest or a stair top on the grid
dry-wash channels meet on the north/south tile edges (same depth, centred)

grid.name: RUIN GRID
grid.note: room plot = cells x 4 m + 0.5 m apron each side; door.position for side cell i = 4*i + 2; its world-space side-cell midpoint is 4*i + 2.5 after the runtime adds 0.5 m (the door anchor 0.4 m in from the room edge lies inside the 1 m wall)
